newsitem.title: UK: EIU cuts Brazil 97/98 exportable coffee estimate.
newsitem.headline: EIU cuts Brazil 97/98 exportable coffee estimate.

text.p: The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) has cut its estimate of Brazil's 1998/98 exportable coffee production to 16.0 million 60-kg bags from its earlier forecast of 17.5 million.
It also revised downward the 1996/97 exportable crop for Brazil to 15.3 million from 16.8 million.

In its second quarter 1997 world commodity forecasts, the London-based group said the 1997/98 (April/March) Indonesian harvest is forecast locally to be at least 10 percent below the 8.0 million bags now estimated for 1996/97.
The EIU also revised downwards world's 1997/98 exportable crop to 78.4 million bags from 79.7 million previously.
This compares with a revised 74.7 million (previously 76.5 million) in 1996/97.
The EIU said Brazil's 1997/98 crop is now expected to fall below the 26-28 million estimated for 1996/97.
Most independent experts dismiss the lowest figures circulating locally of 17-18 million bags, with the consensus favouring 24-25 million.

Brazil's coffee trees have now fully recovered from the 1994 freeze and new plantings are coming on stream, the EIU said, so a cyclical recovery in production is indicated for 1998/99, provided the coffee belt escapes damaging frosts (which can strike from late May) and drought in 1997, it added.
It raised 1998/99 world supply forecast to a record 82 million bags (previously 80.9 million) on the back of Brazil's expansionist strategy and the sharp improvement in prices in recent months.
The EIU said the 1997/98 outlook for robusta production remained good, although it might be less abundant than predicted three months ago, mainly because of dry weather in Indonesia.
It said the revisions indicate the market's return to surplus would now be delayed from 1996/97 to 1997/98.
It also revised upward arabica prices to 157.5 cents a lb for 1997 from 107.8 cents previously. In 1998, the prices will average 133 cents.
World consumption could reach 75.7 million bags in 1997/98 against 74.7 million in 1996/97.
Stocks to consumption ratio is forecast at 73.2 percent in 1998/99 against 67.8 percent in 1997/98 and 65.1 percent in 1996/97. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
